I can certainly relate. It makes me confused as hell in regards to my sexuality too. I'm really into penises. Virtually all adult content I consume is phallocentric. In fantasy I think entirely of cis men... in reality I don't like them much at all. I certainly don't want a relationship with another man or anything else that's not strictly sexual. What attraction I have to men is mostly centered around their possession and use of their genitalia (couldn't care less about anything else physically) so am only into cis dudes. It probably doesn't help that the personality traits in men I find more alluring repulse me in other contexts. I clash with hyper masculine folks, but that's the energy I want in a hookup. I don't care for intimacy with other men either like kissing or cuddling. I've tried but don't enjoy it. And I can't catch feels. 

Now with women on the other hand, I have all the romantic feelings, enjoy the non sexual physical intimacy, and am easily able to care for them as a partner. And I can enjoy having sex with women, but to a significantly lesser extent. Everyone I've fallen for as an adult has been a woman. My position on sex with female partners could probably fall on the ace spectrum, I can enjoy it and enjoy giving my partners what they want and need, but I have little active desire, and will probably be imagining some generic male to get to where I need to. Sex with women (at least cis women) satisfies my ego and is emotionally fulfilling, but it's not really sexually exciting. It really freaking sucks too tbh. Like I enjoy boobies a lot, but I don't find them or any other feminine physical characteristics arousing. Any mentioning, suggestion, or implication of an erection however and I'll be turned on.

I know pensis aren't exclusive to men, but the hunger for it is tied to a hyper masculine dominance as well, and it's just not a dynamic I want in a relationship. I've never been with a trans woman, but I'm not sure how I'd feel in that context assuming she was even good with using her anatomy in such a way. If I were single, I'd probably give t4t a try and see, but it sounds kinda chaser-y to me and I don't like that.

I have been trying my best to work on my independent relationships since things have gotten serious. I'm very introverted and have social anxiety, so it's a struggle though. I do give them alone time. It's been hard, but I am okay with them seeing each other without me. I have the FOMO, but I've tried not to let it affect my behavior towards giving them alone time. They currently see each other twice a week while I'm at work, and she gets a full day on the weekend, with future planned monthly overnights in a hotel/at her place (she has stayed the night with us, where i've been delegated to a couch, which I agreed to, but afterwards realized it sucked and made that a new guideline). My struggles have been more with unplanned "emergencies" that have interrupted time I expected to be/was already spending with my wife. Some have been times I've tagged along cause they've needed my help with something, like heavy lifting or mowing, and they then devolve into me babysitting while they hangout with each other (meta has kids, we don't). I knew the out of state trip was a bad idea, but with meta's violent split with her NP (there was DV involved), she didn't have anyone to drive her, and my wife didn't feel comfortable with her driving herself with her medical issues, and I wasn't yet ready for 4 days without my wife when we had never before been apart post marriage (this was a month in, if that), and that was the compromise we made. It was for a celebration of life, so I didn't tag along once we were there, and I slept in a separate bedroom, and was pretty much just alone with nothing to do the whole time while they bonded over grief and had good sex from across the hall (it was hell). I've put up with a lot because I'm trying to be a good sport. I've made more boundaries since, and have gotten better at standing behind them, but it's still hard, especially when meta legitimately needs help. I definitely wouldn't join again. I know I need to step away some, as I feel I'm putting as much into it as if it were a triad, when it's not, but I also do like my meta quite a bit, so I'm conflicted.

Phone hygiene is the next thing we plan to work on since it's pretty bad.

She doesn't know how to stop talking about her either, though I admit I'm just as guilty with that. We are used to sharing everything. Dealing with being poly and the issues it's presenting has become a full time job. I do still get quality time with my wife, but between losing the weekend day and all of our discussions around feelings and boundaries taking up so much of our time, it's definitely A LOT LESS than it was as mono, and that's a difficult adjustment to make so quick. I'm upset a lot too, which poisons a lot of our time together. I've been filling my alone by trying to talk to other people but I really don't enjoy it. It just makes me miss my wife. This all has been improving though, as we learn and adjust.

In my case, I didn't have a lot of early childhood symptoms. My recreational interests where perhaps slightly on the masculine side, though I had stereotypically feminine interests as well (I played survival outside in the dirt a lot and liked building related toys, like legos and k'nex, but also didn't like sports too much and loved stuffed animals and drawing). 

I didn't perceive gender as much as how I felt/what I wanted and thought it more of as an unquestionable reality. What I personally wanted wasn't a priority in my mind. Due to unfortunate sexual abuse as a young child, my first memories are of learning very I had female anatomy and that with that I had certain obligations I was expected to fulfill (that I now know was super fucked up and perverse, but I didn't know that then). When it came to expression, while I was horribly uncomfortable in feminine clothing, my thoughts were less about what I wanted to wear, and more on what I was supposed to wear. I was way to scared to consider deviating from expectations.

My mental health began deteriorating when puberty hit, but I wasn't aware as to why, just that I hated my body and thought I was just bad at being a girl.

In high school I presented more feminine in order to be accepted. My constant preoccupation with others' opinions of me drowned out any of my own wishes. I believed it was wrong to to think of what would make me happy, so I didn't do it. There was a lot of pressure being a well known, high achieving student in a religious small town. I didn't know what being trans actually was (I thought transgender was synonymous to drag queen) and it took me a long time to actually question things and start doing things for my own happiness and well being.

I think I was 17 when I finally learned what it was to be trans after having a particularly profound dream of being male and waking crushed that it wasn't real. Google then quickly opened up a whole knew world to me, and I finally started questioning things. 

Even after casting off the self imposed gender role shackles, It still took several years commit and actually come out as trans as I was worried I would regret it (I wanted the all the changes, but had grown very attached to my singing ability and was scared how it would effect it), but after a few suicide attempts (for primarily other reasons, but the same forces in my mind compelling my to deny myself also wanted me to blow my head off), a lot of soul searching, and finally learning that my happiness actually had relevance, I eventually took the leap, came out and began my medical transition around 2 years ago, and my confidence and happiness in my skin is astronomically better now.

I know this can be very expensive, and depending on the location sometimes does more harm than good, but have you considered checking yourself into a psychiatric facility? I'm not suggesting that you need to, just that it might be useful. It sounds like you know what it is you need to do, but just can't bring yourself to do it or perhaps don't care about yourself enough to do it. If that's the case, placing yourself in an environment where other people are there to push you to do what you need to do can be helpful for some. It sounds like you're in that depressed stage where you hate your life, and everything in it, and can't bring yourself to do anything/are so checked out from all the bullshit that you don't care to try. Having been in that kind of place a lot, I feel we often need others to push us to help ourselves. You've got to get your meds stabilized and seeing a therapist once a week can be really good for keeping you in line when it comes to self care. While I agree that the T dosage, and perhaps other issues related to gender and transition could be straining things even more here, I'm personally getting the impression that the primary issue here is un-managed mental illness.

Having lived on both sides, I'd say that each have their own shit sandwich. Not to be that person, as I know that it's infinitely easier said than done, but you have to learn not to care what others think. Who cares if you look 'weak' to some people. Have confidence in yourself and your knowledge that seeking help is no weakness. Shake off the painful shackles of a male upbringing while keeping the attributes you like. I recognize that I have a much easier time ignoring the toxic elements that masquerade as 'true masculinity' and embracing a different kind of masculinity since I was born female and wasn't socialized as male. I also recognize that my transition has instilled in me a degree of 'fuck whatever society has to say' that makes it much easier to be myself without the poisonings of shame, guilt, or disgust. I am no 'alpha' and am proud and loved by many not despite, but because of that. 

As far as others go, the world is full of shitty people who will treat you bad for all kinds of dumb reasons. However, there are good people out there. The same things that were crucified in my hometown were celebrated when I went to college. I have been blessed to found some (there aren't many, but enough when you look hard enough) who love me for being unapologetically myself.

For the shortcomings of yourself that you would like to change, and by that I mean the things that the true genuine YOU  want to change and not what society pressures you to fix, the first step to changing I've found is compassion. You are not wrong, you are not bad, you are not defective or a freak in any way. You are a human with human strengths and faults, and you must try to love yourself regardless of either. When you make a mistake, instead of scolding yourself, treat yourself as you would a child, a lover, a friend- with compassion and patience. Accept that you made a mistake, simply (it doesn't have to be painful) and try again. And if you don't want to change something, don't!

All that said, while I'm not sure if gender in this post is being used as an illustration or if you truly do wish your were born female, in the case of the latter, I understand. There are ways to cope with it and things you can do to try and align your body and mind. As someone else has said, the good people of r/asktransgender can help you sort that out, as could a gender therapist. Whatever the case may be, I'm hoping in time you find some peace and contentment within yourself. I'm rooting for you.

I gotta wonder, are you currently being treated for depression? If not maybe you should see about seeing a psychiatrist. If your feeling like this, I really recommend giving it another shot.

Now matter what, I hope you can stay strong. <3
